MIDI is caught either way — noodling with the song stopped is exactly when the good ideas arrive, and Flashback Capture catches those. The audio side added in 11.2 has one condition: you can capture audio only while the project is playing, so leave the transport rolling when the mic is the thing you might want back.

243

Check plugin compatibility after updating

Before you rely on a new version for real work, open your three most important old projects and check every insert. Updates can change how third-party plug-ins load, and finding that out mid-session is expensive.

Section 19

Logic Pro 12 Update.

22 tricks

Logic Pro 12 arrived in January 2026 and it is an Apple silicon release — Intel Macs stop here. The headline additions are the Synth Player and Chord ID, which together change how a track gets arranged. This section covers what is new, plus the upgrade playbook for surviving any major release.

One requirement before anything else

Logic Pro 12 requires an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 15.6 or later. There is no Intel version. If you are still on an Intel machine, Logic Pro 11 is the end of the road — plan around that before you update anything.

What's new in Logic Pro 12

244GAME CHANGER

Synth Player is the third Session Player

Synth Player is not a new Session Player — it is a set of styles inside the Bass Player and Keyboard Player you already have. Create a Bass Player or Keyboard Player track, open the Session Player Editor, and choose a Synth style the same way you choose any other style. The performance still follows the Chord track, so one progression can arrange bass and keys at once.

245

Pick the Synth Keyboard style before you touch anything else

Simple Pad for a sustained harmonic bed, Modulated Pad when you want movement, Rhythmic Chords when the part needs to drive. Same chords, three completely different jobs.

246

Synth Bass ships with three distinct characters

808 Bass for trap-leaning low end, Pump Bass for filtered movement, Sequenced Bass for driving sixteenths. Audition all three before you start editing the pattern.

247

Intensity changes tone, not just level

Pump Bass gets its movement from a modulated ducking effect, and you can shape it directly: in the Session Player Editor click the Details button, then drag the Amount knob vertically to change how hard it pumps and the Shape knob to change the curve of the duck. It is the fastest way to make a bassline build without drawing a single automation point.

248

Point Synth Player at a third-party synth

The performance engine and the sound source are separate. Synth Player can drive any Audio Unit, and external hardware too, so you keep the chord-following performance and choose your own sound.

249GAME CHANGER

Chord ID reads chords off audio, not just MIDI

Drag in a guitar demo, a piano take or a rough bounce and Chord ID analyses it and writes the progression to the Chord track in seconds. It is the fastest route from an idea to a working arrangement.

250

Chord ID gets the harmonic rhythm, not just the chords

Chord ID writes what it finds straight onto the Chord track — drag an audio or MIDI region onto the Chord track and Logic analyses it and adds the chords it contains as a chord group. Play it back against the source before you build on it; the Chord track's Change Display Only mode lets you correct any chord that does not match what you are hearing without altering playback.

251GAME CHANGER

Everything downstream follows the Chord track

Once Chord ID has populated the Chord track, other tracks can lock to it. Apple: "By following the Chord track, multiple tracks — such as tracks using Step Sequencer, Session Player tracks, and other software instrument tracks — can play in sync harmonically." Set a Session Player region to follow with Control-click > Chords > Follow Global Chord Track; set a Step Sequencer pattern to follow by choosing Chord Track, which renames the note rows to chord degrees. One analysis pass can arrange several parts at once.

252

Run Chord ID on your own old bounces

The fastest way to rebuild a session you have lost is to drag the bounce in, let Chord ID read the changes, and start again from a chord track you know is correct.

253

Preview sound packs before you download them

The rebuilt Sound Library lets you look a pack over before you commit — click Preview on a pack to see what is in it, then Get to download it. It is also where you reclaim space: select an installed pack and click Delete. The total space used by all installed packs is shown at the top of the list, with each pack's size beside it.

254

Re-run Mastering Assistant on older masters

Mastering Assistant is worth re-running on an older master after any major update. Reanalyse the mix on the master bus, then A/B the result against the version you signed off on before you call it finished — Apple's character presets (Clean, Valve, Punch, Transparent) give you four quick comparisons at once.

Before you update

255GAME CHANGER

Logic Pro 12 drops Intel Macs entirely

It requires an Apple silicon Mac and macOS 15.6 or later. If you are on Intel, Logic Pro 11 is the last version you can run — check your machine before you plan an upgrade.

256GAME CHANGER

Never update in the middle of a paid project

The one rule that matters. Finish and deliver, then update. A new version halfway through a mix is a self‑inflicted deadline problem.

257

Keep the previous version installed alongside the new one

Keep the outgoing version before you update, using Apple's own procedure: make a folder inside Applications named for the version (for example "Logic Pro 11.1.2"), select Logic Pro and choose File > Compress "Logic Pro", then move the resulting Logic Pro.zip into that folder. If the new version gives you trouble, unzip that copy and drag it into Applications and you are back where you were.

258

Back up your key commands, templates and channel strip settings

Key commands are the only one of these that lives in your user Library. Open the Key Commands window (Option-K), choose Options > Export Key Commands, and save the file somewhere safe — the dialog defaults to ~/Library/Application Support/Logic/Key Commands. Your templates and channel strip settings live somewhere else entirely: ~/Music/Audio Music Apps/Project Templates and ~/Music/Audio Music Apps/Channel Strip Settings. Copy those two folders as well.

259

Consolidate and archive your three most important projects

File > Project Management > Consolidate on each, then copy them to a separate drive. If the new version changes something, you have untouched originals.

260

Check your critical third‑party plugins against the new version first

Plugin developers lag major DAW releases. Check their compatibility pages before you update, not after.

261

Note your current I/O and buffer settings

Screenshot your Audio settings before you update — output device, input device and I/O buffer size. It takes five seconds, and if anything about your setup looks different afterwards you can restore the exact configuration you were working with instead of guessing at it.

262

Update macOS and Logic separately, a week apart

If something breaks, you want to know which of the two did it.

After you update

263

Read the new Key Commands list for additions

Open the Key Commands window after every update — Logic Pro > Key Commands > Edit, or Option-K — and read through it for commands you have not seen before. New features arrive with new commands, many of them unassigned by default, and this is the only place they announce themselves.

264

Test your bounce path end to end before you need it

Bounce a short section to every format you deliver in. Export bugs are the ones that bite at the worst possible moment.

265

Give yourself a deliberate hour to explore

Not on a project. Open a scratch session and use every new feature once. An hour of play beats a month of accidental discovery.

That’s the 265.

Take what is useful and go and finish the song. Come back whenever you get stuck — every section is one tap away.
